What actually came back

The recurring failure is the same one every time. Ask a model to merge M and B onto a shared stem and it fuses the M’s right leg into the B, which leaves a shape that reads NB, not MB. Look at 48, 41, 32, 27 — the construction is elegant and the letter is wrong. That is not a prompt you can fix; it is what a shared stem does to an M.

It also ignored “geometric sans-serif” almost everywhere. Nearly all of these are serifed or slabbed, which fights Jost on the rest of the site. The first twelve were generated before I added that phrase, and adding it moved the needle less than expected.

What is genuinely useful: 06 and 50, the blueprint pair, because the dimension-callout treatment is the spec-sheet voice the site already speaks in — that is worth stealing as a device even though the letterform under it is wrong. 12, letterpress, for the framing. 03 and 04 for the silhouette test. None of these are traceable into a mark without redrawing the letters, so treat the whole grid as reference.

Coded50 marks · live type, not pictures

Every one of these is real type and CSS in your palette, so anything you point at ships the same day. Hover a tile for its motion. 16px drops all fifty to favicon size at once so you can see which ones die; Ink flips the ground.
